findings.claim: Older admitted EventStore packages lack the new recovery snapshot API
findings.evidence: Directory.Build.targets still admits 4.0.4/4.1.0/4.2.0/5.0.1 while TenantAggregate unconditionally uses ProjectionSnapshotLimits. Four dotnet-inspect API diffs confirm the type was added in 5.1.0. Recovery was introduced by 6fcff842a8e48fc843d7b2df942d369f99f92b6b; package selections are explicitly excluded from this timeout repair.

findings.claim: Authentication can change during user-context corroboration
findings.evidence: Carried from Blind 7 and B1/E1 of the 2026-11-13 review: the same getter remains after the only generation check. The prior boundary reproduction and outstanding production-accessor qualification retain their disposition; do not append another deferral.

findings.claim: Rejection-only tenant state receives a different recovery refusal
findings.evidence: TenantState starts with an empty TenantId; its TenantNotFoundRejection Apply leaves it empty, and SDK replay constructs a state object. RefreshTenantAccess checks foreign TenantId before checking for an uncreated aggregate, so a subsequent attempt returns InsufficientPermissionsRejection. This belongs to later recovery commit 6fcff842a8e48fc843d7b2df942d369f99f92b6b.

findings.claim: Twenty-second credential expires during twenty-five-second readiness wait
findings.evidence: The reported timing does not cause the claimed rejection: the actual JwtBearerAuthenticationContract sets a sixty-second clock skew and the unnamed standard readiness allowance is thirty seconds. A token expiring five seconds before dispatch is still inside that effective lifetime. No refusal beyond the effective validated lifetime was demonstrated; do not add credential reacquisition from this example.

findings.claim: C# wrapper can truncate the browser progress checkpoint
findings.evidence: RetainBrowserProgressAsync reads the retained snapshot then writes directly to the same path with File.WriteAllTextAsync. Interruption during that write can destroy the complete checkpoint. This later evidence-wrapper change is owned by 7066cbaeff0a34624250542eb4954fbb8c623027, outside the native timeout behavior.

findings.claim: Failure diagnostics can outlive the functional browser deadline
findings.evidence: The failure path directly awaits captureFocus/captureReadiness; those execute page evaluation without a separate cancellation race. A wedged renderer can therefore keep failure cleanup pending until the outer test timeout. The original baseline already contains the unbounded captureReadiness call; no native budget increase introduced it.

findings.claim: Concurrent Firefox evidence driver labels a longer poll loop as thirty seconds
findings.evidence: The unrelated untracked fix-firefox-route-focus-ci-2026-11-15/verify.sh loops 120 times with a one-second HTTP timeout plus a 250ms pause. That is not a thirty-second elapsed-time bound. Preserve this other workstream and its evidence; no historical evidence file is edited.

findings.claim: Live corpus credential creation has no total corpus or encoded-token limit
findings.evidence: AuthenticatedRouteState.CreateCorpusReadTokenAsync limits each page to 100 but continues for any fresh cursor, growing exactIds and cursors until caller cancellation. A sufficiently large valid corpus also becomes one JWT and then a browser session. This is separate scoped-live-credential work introduced by 5db9648cfd0456896c1c549dcd1021f4c216bf2d.

findings.claim: Recovery command tests omit exact default snapshot boundaries
findings.evidence: The cited command tests cover ordinary/oversized snapshots, not exactly 4096/4097 entries. SDK ProjectionSnapshotLimitsTests already exercise exact encoded-byte acceptance and one-byte excess; the command uses the shared default and a direct greater-than count check. No boundary defect was demonstrated, and extra command scaffolding is not a direct correction; reject this negligible testing improvement under the low-finding rule.

findings.claim: New recovery operation lacks a full delivery/convergence regression
findings.evidence: Searches find RefreshTenantAccess in structural/generated-controller and aggregate tests, but no command-gateway live delivery test in the authenticated route suite. Add persisted-event and consumer-convergence coverage in the separate recovery feature from 6fcff842a8e48fc843d7b2df942d369f99f92b6b; this timeout intent excludes business-runtime launches.

findings.claim: Seventy-five-second mocked detail overstates the production API allowance
findings.evidence: DefaultEnrichmentDeadlineAcceptsAuthoritativeDetailAtSupportedElapsedTimes tests the injectable whole-page timer, not an end-to-end per-call service guarantee. The independent actual API transport tests enforce the fifty-second per-call timeout and caller cancellation. The ninety-second aggregate page allowance does not extend that caller SLA; no production budget defect follows from the unit seam.
Carried from the same 2026-11-13 Blind 7/B1/E1 row as B2, with the same location and claim. Preserve the recorded production-accessor qualification limit; no repeated patch or ledger entry.
